1998-09-01: David Bowie launched BowieNet, his own internet service provider offering subscription-based dial-up access and a dedicated David Bowie website.
1999-05-14: Eidos announced a partnership with David Bowie and Iman, with their first project, the video game Omikron: The Nomad Soul, featuring music and songs composed by Bowie and a character based on him, set for release in October.

2002-05-31: David Bowie releases his 27th studio album, Heathen, which achieves a balance between experimental and pop elements.
2002-06-05: David Bowie's new album Heathen, produced by Tony Visconti, is generating excitement and being described as his best album since Scary Monsters in 1980.
2002-06-09: David Bowie faces a lawsuit from producer Gus Dudgeon, who claims he is owed millions in royalty payments spanning 30 years for his work on the 1969 song 'Space Oddity'.
2002-06-17: David Bowie summoned The Legendary Stardust Cowboy to play a rare British show at the South Bank's Meltdown festival.
2002-06-30: David Bowie performs a closing gig at the Meltdown festival at the Festival Hall, featuring complete performances of the albums Low and Heathen.
2002-07-06: David Bowie performs a concert at the Royal Festival Hall in London as part of his Meltdown Festival, featuring a performance of his album Low followed by material from Heathen.
2002-07-30: David Bowie is shortlisted for the Mercury music prize for his album Heathen.
2003-06-27: In a radio program, poet Simon Armitage and musicologist Allan Moore discussed David Bowie as Ziggy Stardust, analyzing the lyrics and music of the song.
2003-09-10: David Bowie performs a concert at an exclusive London venue that is beamed via computer to 68 fan-packed cinemas in 22 countries.
2003-09-12: David Bowie releases his 26th album, Reality, which explores the concept of reality.
2003-09-13: David Bowie releases his twenty-sixth album, Reality.
2003-11-16: David Bowie performs a UK arena concert featuring both new material from Reality and revived older hits, including Rebel Rebel, Fame, The Man Who Sold The World, Life On Mars, Changes, Under Pressure, China Girl, Sunday, Five Years, I'm Afraid Of Americans, Ashes to Ashes, and Ziggy Stardust.
2004-06-25: A 30th anniversary edition of David Bowie's album Diamond Dogs is released.
2004-07-08: David Bowie underwent an emergency heart operation for an acutely blocked artery after falling ill following a concert in Germany.
2006-01-16: A blog post mentions David Bowie's Major Tom songs as part of a space and sci-fi music theme.
2006-02-15: Paul Weller is set to receive a lifetime achievement award at the Brits, following past recipients such as David Bowie, who received the award in 1996.
2006-03-10: A review of David Bowie's 1983 Serious Moonlight concert film is published, discussing his early-1980s mainstream persona and the tour's staging.
2006-05-31: David Bowie made a surprise appearance during the final two songs of David Gilmour's Royal Albert Hall performance.
2007-01-01: David Bowie is noted to be turning 60 in just over a week, with the Observer Review paying tribute to him and examining his lasting influence on today's music stars.
2007-03-16: A review of David Bowie's 1975 album Young Americans is published, discussing its shift into black music and its influence.
2007-08-31: David Bowie is reported to be set to appear in Doctor Who as an alien.
2007-11-14: A 1976 mugshot of David Bowie, taken by New York police after his arrest for marijuana possession in Rochester, is reported to be for sale on eBay.
2008-04-17: David Bowie's October 20, 1972 Santa Monica Civic Auditorium concert is to be officially released as "David Bowie, Live Santa Monica '72" on June 30.
2008-06-26: A former radio broadcast of David Bowie's 1972 Ziggy Stardust tour is released in a box set with original reviews.
2008-10-14: David Bowie's compilation album iSELECT: BOWIE, originally a free CD with the Mail on Sunday, is scheduled for a general commercial release with two semi-exclusive tracks.
2008-11-28: David Bowie previously proclaimed the Human League "the future of rock'n'roll" after bursting into their dressing room at a London gig in late 1979.
2011-06-06: David Bowie's 1975 single Golden Years is reissued as an iPhone app allowing fans to remix the song.
2011-10-12: An article reflects on David Bowie's 1983 return with the song "Let's Dance," noting the anticipation and mixed fan reactions to his more accessible, commercially successful persona.
2012-01-09: A graphic novel prequel to the 1986 film Labyrinth, which featured David Bowie as Jareth the Goblin King, is announced for release later in the year, with illustrator Brian Froud overseeing character design and Archaia editor Stephen Christy saying he is talking with Bowie about possibly contributing songs or an introduction.
2012-09-04: The V&A announces the first museum retrospective of David Bowie, titled "David Bowie is," scheduled to run from 23 March to 28 July 2013.
2013-01-08: David Bowie announced a musical comeback, ending a 10-year silence.
David Bowie released his first single in a decade, with an album, The Next Day, announced to follow in March.
David Bowie's album The Next Day, featuring cover art by Jonathan Barnbrook, is discussed as a design masterstroke that subverts his iconic album artwork.
2013-01-11: David Bowie released a surprise comeback single, generating media excitement.
2013-02-25: David Bowie released the single "Where Are We Now?" on his 66th birthday, breaking a decade of silence and preceding the album "The Next Day."
2013-03-16: David Bowie's album The Next Day, released the previous week, went straight to No 1 on iTunes and was likely to become his first No 1 album in the official UK charts since 1993, while advance ticket sales for the V&A exhibition David Bowie Is broke museum records.
A radio documentary, I Dressed Ziggy Stardust, about David Bowie's significance to teenage girls from British Asian families, is scheduled to air on BBC Radio 4.
2013-03-17: The David Bowie exhibition "David Bowie Is" becomes the fastest-selling event in the Victoria and Albert Museum's history.
2013-03-18: David Bowie's first album in a decade, The Next Day, reached No. 1 in its first week of release, becoming the fastest-selling album of the year.
2013-03-22: David Bowie's new album reached No 1 in its first week of release, his first time topping the albums chart in 20 years.
2013-03-23: An exhibition titled "David Bowie Is" opens at the V&A in London.
2013-04-20: David Bowie is releasing a collectible 7-inch vinyl version of "The Stars (Are Out Tonight)" / "Where Are We Now" and a reissue of the 1973 single "Drive-In Saturday" as part of Record Store Day releases.
2013-05-07: An exhibition of Brian Duffy's David Bowie photographs opens at Leeds' White Cloth Gallery.
2013-05-11: An explicit version of the video for David Bowie's new release, The Next Day, was in the news.
2013-10-01: A new version of the exhibition David Bowie Is opens at the Art Gallery of Ontario, with curators revealing a list of Bowie's top 100 must-read books.
2013-10-21: David Bowie fails to win any prizes at the Q awards despite being nominated in six categories.
2013-10-30: Four new David Bowie songs appeared on YouTube and a previously unseen video for "Love Is Lost" was unveiled at the Mercury music prize ceremony.
2014-02-19: David Bowie wins British male solo artist at the 2014 Brits and, in a proxy acceptance speech read by Kate Moss, asks Scotland not to vote for independence.
2014-02-20: David Bowie was confirmed to be from Mars at the Brit Awards 2014.
2014-04-19: David Bowie will release two limited-edition 7-inch picture discs, "Rock 'n' Roll Suicide" in the UK and "1984" in North America, for Record Store Day.
2014-05-14: Commander Chris Hadfield's viral video of his cover of David Bowie's "Space Oddity," performed aboard the International Space Station, was made private after the one-year permission from Bowie's representatives expired.
2014-05-20: A specially curated Berlin version of the David Bowie Is exhibition, focusing on Bowie's cathartic years in divided Berlin, opens at the Martin-Gropius-Bau.
2014-07-26: Susan Sarandon reveals she had a sexual relationship with David Bowie around the time they worked together on the film The Hunger.
2014-08-10: The David Bowie Is exhibition runs at the Martin-Gropius-Bau in Berlin until this date.
2014-10-12: David Bowie released the new track "Sue (Or in a Season of Crime)" as part of his greatest hits collection Nothing Has Changed.
2014-11-13: A documentary tribute film about the V&A exhibition "David Bowie Is" is reviewed, staging dramatised tableaux and featuring interviews with Bowie scholars, collaborators, and fans.
2015-01-08: David Bowie is to release his new album Blackstar, which was inspired by Kendrick Lamar and features LCD's James Murphy.
2015-04-02: David Bowie announces he is co-writing a new stage musical, Lazarus, with playwright Enda Walsh, featuring new songs and inspired by The Man Who Fell to Earth.
2015-04-04: New York Theater Workshop announces it will stage Lazarus, a musical based on The Man Who Fell to Earth featuring new songs from David Bowie, later in 2015.
2015-04-14: Director Ivo van Hove reveals that David Bowie's forthcoming musical Lazarus will feature new songs about love and violence, with Bowie not appearing on stage.
2015-06-26: Tony Visconti and Woody Woodmansey, with Glenn Gregory, perform a concert revisiting David Bowie’s music, noting Bowie is not present because he did not want to be.
2015-07-02: David Bowie announced the release of Five Years 1969-1973, a box set featuring a previously unavailable 1971 version of Holy Holy.
2015-07-16: An exhibition titled "David Bowie Is," featuring unprecedented access to the David Bowie archive, premieres at the Australian Centre for the Moving Image in Melbourne and runs until 1 November.
2015-07-24: The Bombay Royale performs at ACMI as part of late-night events coinciding with the David Bowie Is exhibition.
2015-08-18: A Kingston University professor begins spending a year living as David Bowie, adopting the star's personas, habits, and reading to understand his work.
2015-09-25: David Bowie announces the release of Five Years 1969-1973, the first in a series of career-spanning box sets.
2015-10-13: David Bowie's booking agent John Giddings said Bowie has decided to retire from touring.
2015-10-26: David Bowie announces that he will release his new album Blackstar on his 69th birthday, with a single of the same name preceding it on 2015-11-20.
2015-12-07: David Bowie's new musical Lazarus, featuring his songs and co-written by him, opened at New York Theatre Workshop.
2015-12-08: David Bowie's musical Lazarus, with songs by Bowie and directed by Ivo van Hove, opens off-Broadway.
2015-12-10: A box set titled Five Years 1969-1973, covering David Bowie's Mick Ronson era, is reviewed.
2016-01-08: David Bowie released his final album, Blackstar.

David Bowie's former band members and collaborators are to perform a tribute concert at Brixton Academy on what would have been his 70th birthday, with further shows planned in New York, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Tokyo.
2016-01-10: David Bowie died at age 69 following an 18-month burst of creativity that included the release of his final album Blackstar two days before his death.
2016-01-11: David Bowie died, prompting tributes including a Holy Holy concert where longtime producer Tony Visconti and drummer Mick Woodmansey reflected on his death.
David Bowie's death prompted fans worldwide to gather and pay tribute, with mourners laying flowers at locations including Brixton, Beckenham, Berlin, and New York.
UK national newspapers published extensive front-page tributes and leading articles praising David Bowie following his death.
David Bowie's final single "Lazarus" and the New York theatre work he co-wrote are discussed, reflecting his relationship with America.
David Bowie's death was announced, prompting tributes including from David Cameron.
Broadcasters including BBC1, Channel 4, BBC2, and Radio 2 altered their schedules to air tributes to David Bowie following his death.
The Victoria and Albert Museum's David Bowie exhibition opened its doors at the Groninger Museum in the Netherlands for fans to view and sign a book of condolence following Bowie's death at age 69.
2016-01-12: Henry Rollins delivers a spoken-word tribute to David Bowie during a performance, recounting a 1997 encounter when Bowie, a fan of Rollins, quoted his books and later connected him with Lou Reed.
David Bowie's death is mourned, with reflection on how his 1983 "Let's Dance" music video, featuring Aboriginal performers, highlighted Australia's Indigenous struggle.
Sales of David Bowie's final album Blackstar soared and tribute shows and memorial events were announced following his death.
2016-01-13: Holy Holy, featuring Woody Woodmansey and Tony Visconti, performed a David Bowie tribute concert in the wake of Bowie's death, with Visconti telling the crowd there was no better way to work through grief than through music.
2016-01-14: David Bowie's family said they are overwhelmed by the reaction to his death and are making arrangements for a private ceremony to celebrate his memory.
David Bowie's longest-serving pianist Mike Garson remembers his friend, reflecting on Bowie's death and their career together.
2016-01-15: Following David Bowie's death, his album Blackstar debuts at No 1 on the UK album charts, making it his 10th chart-topping LP, amid over half a million record sales.
2016-01-22: Reports claimed Labyrinth, starring David Bowie, would be rebooted, but screenwriter Nicole Perlman denied any involvement in a remake.
2016-02-02: Lady Gaga is set to perform a tribute to David Bowie at the Grammy awards, with the performance to be musically directed by Nile Rodgers.
2016-02-06: The 1991 film The Linguini Incident, starring David Bowie, is reissued on DVD.
Lady Gaga is set to perform a tribute to David Bowie at the Grammy awards ceremony, a decision debated in the article.
2016-02-13: David Bowie's song "Drive in Saturday" is included in a list of science-themed songs, noted for its sci-fi premise set in 2033.
2016-02-22: Iggy Pop performed a David Bowie tribute at the Tibet House benefit concert at Carnegie Hall, performing Bowie's song "Jean Genie" and joining the cast on "Tonight," a song he wrote with Bowie.
2016-02-25: David Bowie's son Duncan Jones thanked Brits for a "beautiful" tribute performance of Life on Mars by Lorde and Bowie's backing band.
2016-02-28: David Bowie was remembered in the In Memoriam segment of the Oscars ceremony.
2016-03-17: David Bowie's record producer Tony Visconti, in his SXSW keynote, said the next David Bowie lives somewhere in the world but is not getting a shot or being financed.
2016-05-11: An original UK pressing of David Bowie's second album, later retitled Space Oddity, became the most expensive record ever sold on Discogs, fetching $6,826.
2016-06-03: David Bowie is among the famous past and present residents and students of south London celebrated in an exhibition opening at the National Portrait Gallery.
2016-06-10: Thousands of music fans will be invited to wear masks of David Bowie at the Isle of Wight festival as the first of a series of tributes to the late singer at events around the UK this summer.
2016-06-16: Glastonbury festival reveals plans to commemorate David Bowie, including a giant Ziggy Stardust lightning bolt sculpture on the Pyramid stage and a 50-piece orchestral performance of Philip Glass's fourth symphony based on Bowie's album Heroes.
2016-07-22: A previously unreleased David Bowie album, The Gouster, recorded in 1974, is set to be released later in 2016 as part of the box set Who Can I Be Now? (1974-1976).
2016-07-25: A new David Bowie box set, Who Can I Be Now?, compiling unreleased material, remastered albums, and live recordings from his 1974–76 American phase, is announced for release on 23 September.
2016-07-30: A David Bowie Prom tribute concert was held, featuring reworked Bowie songs performed by various artists.
2016-08-22: A plaque commemorating David Bowie's time living in Berlin was unveiled in the city's Schöneberg district.
2016-09-08: Nicolas Roeg’s film The Man Who Fell to Earth, starring David Bowie as Thomas Newton, is rereleased after 40 years.
2016-09-20: Dozens of paintings, sculptures and design pieces from David Bowie's art collection go on display in Los Angeles as part of a global tour before Sotheby's auctions the entire collection in London in November.
2016-09-22: A review is published of the box set David Bowie: Who Can I Be Now? (1974-1976), which traces Bowie's career from Diamond Dogs to Station to Station and includes The Gouster, a reconstruction of an early version of Young Americans.
2016-10-21: An album featuring David Bowie's final recordings, Lazarus Cast Album, is released.
2016-10-22: An album featuring the last studio recordings made by David Bowie goes on sale this week, ahead of the opening of the Lazarus stage show next month.

2016-11-01: Around 400 artworks and other items once owned by the late David Bowie go on free public display at Sotheby's in London before being sold in three auctions later in November.
2016-11-04: BBC2 announces a documentary, David Bowie: The Last Five Years, exploring Bowie’s final projects and featuring previously unheard vocals and unseen archive footage, to be broadcast in January.
2016-11-10: The first items from David Bowie's personal art collection were sold at auction in London, fetching more than £24m.
2016-12-31: Sydney's New Year's Eve midnight fireworks display included a tribute honoring David Bowie, along with Prince and Gene Wilder.
2017-01-08: A new David Bowie EP, No Plan, was released to mark what would have been the star's 70th birthday, and a charity concert was held at Brixton Academy.
2017-01-09: A David Bowie tribute concert celebrating his 70th birthday was held, featuring his backing musicians, collaborators, and friends performing his songs.
2017-01-17: A one-man show inspired by David Bowie, "From Ibiza to the Norfolk Broads," is performed at the Arts Centre in Swindon.
2017-01-31: A graphic novel titled "Haddon Hall: When David Invented Bowie" by Nejib, depicting David Bowie's life at Haddon Hall from 1969 to 1972, is reviewed.
2017-03-02: A concert film documenting David Bowie's retirement of his Ziggy Stardust alter ego at the Hammersmith Apollo in 1973 is rereleased into cinemas for a single-night show.
